brief.t: Started in 2001 as a joint venture of State Bank of India and France's BNP Paribas Cardif; listed on NSE and BSE in October 2017. SBI is the promoter with about 55% of the shares; BNP Paribas Cardif cut its stake to 0.2% in 2021.
Sells term (protection), savings, ULIP, pension and annuity plans. SBI's branches (bancassurance) bring in about 53% of new business (APE); agents and other partners bring the rest.
Amit Jhingran, a career SBI banker, has been MD & CEO since 2023; the board re-appointed him for a term up to 31 Jan 2027. SBI Chairman Challa Sreenivasulu Setty is the Chairman.
FY 2025-26: gross written premium crossed ₹1 lakh crore (₹1,01,290 cr, +19%), but net profit grew only 2% to ₹2,470 crore. VNB margin was 27.5%.
H1 FY27 (Apr–Sep 2026): profit ₹1,274 crore (+17%), APE ₹11,746 crore (+18%), VNB margin 27.9%. The removal of GST on policies cut H1 profit by about ₹530 crore.

timeline.t: Began as a joint venture of State Bank of India and BNP Paribas Cardif.
IPO: shares listed on NSE and BSE.
BNP Paribas Cardif sold most of its remaining stake, keeping 0.2%.

Gross written premium crossed ₹1 lakh crore for FY 2025-26.
Tie-up with J&K Bank to sell SBI Life plans through its branches.

model.how: SBI Life collects premiums from customers, mostly through SBI branches and its own agents, and invests the money (₹5.27 lakh crore AUM) in government bonds, corporate debt and shares. It pays claims, maturity and surrender amounts, and earns a profit over the life of each policy. Term (protection) and guaranteed (non-par) plans earn the highest margins; ULIPs are the biggest product.
flow: Sells policies via SBI branches, agents, brokers and online
Invests in bonds and shares (AUM ₹5.27 lakh cr)
Pays claims and maturities; keeps the margin over many years

points: GST on individual life policies was removed from 22 Sep 2025. Customers pay less, but insurers lost tax credits, which cut SBI Life's H1 FY27 profit by about ₹530 crore.
Bank-backed insurers (SBI Life, HDFC Life, ICICI Prudential Life) depend heavily on their parent bank's branches; IRDAI is now reviewing distribution costs and commissions.
Big theme for interviews: growing high-margin protection and non-par plans when customers prefer market-linked ULIPs.

glossary.Net profit: What is left after all costs and taxes. The company's final earnings.
glossary.Revenue: Total money earned from the business in a period, before costs.
glossary.Dividend: Part of the profit paid to shareholders, per share.
glossary.Attrition: The % of employees who leave in a year. Also called employee turnover.
glossary.IPO: Initial Public Offering: when a company first sells its shares to the public.
glossary.Market share: A company's sales as a % of the total sales of its industry.
glossary.Consolidated: Figures for the company together with its subsidiaries. 'Standalone' means the parent company alone.
glossary.BRSR: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: an official yearly report on people, environment and governance that big listed companies must publish.
glossary.KYC: Know Your Customer: checking a customer's identity before opening an account or selling a product.
glossary.IRDAI: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India: the regulator of all insurance companies.
glossary.Premium: The money a customer pays to buy an insurance policy.
glossary.Gross written premium: Total premium collected in a period, from new and renewing policies.
glossary.New business premium: Premium from policies sold for the first time in the period.
glossary.Renewal premium: Premium paid by existing customers to keep their policies going.
glossary.APE: Annualised Premium Equivalent: a standard measure of new sales. Regular premiums count fully, single premiums count 10%.
glossary.VNB: Value of New Business: the expected future profit (today's value) from policies sold in the period. A key measure for life insurers.
glossary.VNB margin: VNB as a % of APE. Shows how profitable new sales are.
glossary.Embedded value: The value of a life insurer today: its net worth plus the present value of future profits from existing policies.
glossary.Persistency: The % of customers who keep paying premiums after a set time (e.g. 13th month, 61st month). Higher is better.
glossary.Solvency ratio: Available capital compared with the capital the regulator requires. IRDAI's minimum is 150% (1.5 times).
glossary.AUM: Assets Under Management: the money the insurer invests on behalf of policyholders and shareholders.
glossary.Protection: Pure risk cover such as term insurance: pays only if something happens, cheap premium, high profit margin.
glossary.ULIP: Unit Linked Insurance Plan: part insurance, part market investment. Returns depend on markets.
glossary.Par / Non-par: Participating (par) policies share profits through bonuses; non-participating (non-par) policies give fixed, guaranteed benefits.
glossary.Annuity: A product that pays a regular income, usually after retirement, in return for a lump sum.
glossary.Bancassurance: Selling insurance through a bank's branches and customers. A main channel for bank-backed insurers.
glossary.Agency: Selling insurance through individual commission-based agents.
glossary.Surrender: When a customer exits a policy early and gets back part of the money.
glossary.Claim settlement ratio: The % of claims an insurer pays out of those it receives. Higher means more claims paid.
glossary.GST on insurance: Tax charged on premiums. From 22 Sep 2025 the government removed GST on individual life and health policies.
glossary.Bima Sugam: An IRDAI online marketplace planned to let customers buy, compare and service insurance in one place.
glossary.Indian embedded value: SBI Life's reported embedded value, calculated under Indian Embedded Value principles and checked by an outside actuary.
glossary.Individual rated premium: New individual premium where single premiums count only 10%. Used to compare market share among life insurers.
glossary.Promoter: The main owner that controls a listed company. SBI is SBI Life's promoter with about 55% of shares.
glossary.Ind AS: Indian accounting standards based on global IFRS. IRDAI let insurers delay adopting them by one year.
glossary.Joint venture: A company set up and owned together by two partners, here SBI and BNP Paribas Cardif.

Role knowledge, the company and HR questions

Finance.q: SBI Life's APE grew 18% in H1 FY27 but profit grew 17%. Why does profit lag new sales in life insurance?
Finance.a: A life insurer books most of the cost of a new policy (commission, setting up) in year one, while profit comes over many years. VNB, ₹3,274 crore (+19%), is the better measure of the value of new sales.

Finance.q: What is a solvency ratio and what is SBI Life's?
Finance.a: Capital available compared with what IRDAI requires; the minimum is 1.5. SBI Life's was 1.97 in Sep 2026.

Finance.q: How did the GST change affect SBI Life?
Finance.a: GST on individual policies was removed from Sep 2025. Customers pay less, but the insurer lost input tax credits on its costs, which cut H1 FY27 profit by about ₹530 crore.

Marketing.q: How would you get more young people to buy term insurance from SBI Life?
Marketing.a: Use SBI's app and branch data to target first-time earners, explain cover in simple language and rupee terms, and use digital campaigns and quick online buying.

Marketing.q: Why does SBI Life push protection and non-par plans when ULIPs sell more?
Marketing.a: Protection and guaranteed plans have higher margins and do not depend on stock markets; protection NBP grew 46% in H1 FY27.

HR.q: How would you reduce early attrition of new insurance agents?
HR.a: Better selection, a mentor for the first 6 months, small early wins with warm leads, regular training and quick commission payouts.

Sales.a: Ask about my family and loans, show how much cover I need, compare the yearly premium to a small monthly cost, and stress that claims are paid (SBI Life's death claim settlement ratio was 99.1% in H1 FY27).

Operations.q: Why does persistency matter, and how can operations improve it?
Operations.a: Insurers earn over many years, so lapsed policies lose future profit. Auto-debit, reminders, easy online payment and good service raise persistency. SBI Life's 13th month persistency was 85.8% in Q2 FY27 (premium basis).

Other.q: What is bancassurance and why is it important for SBI Life?
Other.a: Selling insurance through bank branches. SBI's branches give SBI Life about 53% of its new business (APE).

interview.why_us: SBI Life brings life insurance to families across India through State Bank of India's branches, its agents and new partners like J&K Bank. It has crossed ₹1 lakh crore in yearly premium and manages over ₹5 lakh crore of policyholders' money. It is growing new business fast while keeping margins strong, and is pushing protection so more families are properly covered. I want to contribute to [your role] in that mission.
ask: How is SBI Life growing agency and other channels alongside SBI branches?
How will the IRDAI review of distribution costs change the way products are sold?
What does success look like for a new joiner in the first six months?

gd.t: Should banks be allowed to push their own group's insurance products to customers?
gd.for: It brings insurance to millions through trusted branches at low cost.
gd.against: Risk of mis-selling and less choice for customers.

gd.t: Was removing GST on life insurance a good move?
gd.for: Lower premiums make cover more affordable and support 'Insurance for All by 2047'.
gd.against: Insurers lose tax credits, which can hurt profits or keep prices from falling fully.

avoid: Don't say BNP Paribas Cardif is still a joint-venture partner; it cut its stake to 0.2% in 2021. SBI is the promoter.
Don't confuse Q2 profit (₹549 cr) with H1 profit (₹1,274 cr).
Don't judge a life insurer only on net profit; talk about APE, VNB margin, persistency and solvency.
